subject: URGENT: BlueParcel production P0 — KV prefetch clobbering causing 5xx and p99 spikes
messages:
From: Samir Shah <samir@blueparcel.com>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Cc: BlueParcel EngOps <ops@blueparcel.com>, Marta Rodriguez <marta@blueparcel.com>
Date: 2026-11-18T07:21:00Z
Subject: Production P0: 500 spikes + throughput collapse (many requests timing out)

Hi Kimberly,

We're seeing a major regression starting ~07:10 UTC across our europe cluster: request 5xx rate jumped from ~0.1% to ~12% and p99 latency shot to 4.3s. Throughput looks uneven — a small set of prefixes dominates and a lot of requests time out with 502/504. Attaching traces and a small sample of request ids.

Impact: checkout flow for ~4% of users; our monitoring has fired a high-sev page. We believe this started after the rolling update you did to the latest KV prefetching profile earlier this morning. Can you confirm?

Attachments: blueparcel-error-sample-logs.txt, bp-request-id-trace.json

We need immediate mitigation; please advise steps you can take to stop the surge / reduce errors.

— Samir
Principal SRE, BlueParcel

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@blueparcel.com>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T07:34:00Z
Subject: Re: Production P0: 500 spikes + throughput collapse (many requests timing out)

Samir —

Thank you for the heads up and the traces. We're investigating now. Initial triage from the runtime indicates heavy KV eviction activity on the priority lane (hot prefixes) and aggressive prefetching churn; that matches increased 5xx and p99. I'm spinning up an emergency hotlane cap increase and will temporarily reduce aggressive prefetch windows to limit clobbering.

Immediate actions (in progress):
- Reduce prefetch window from 200ms -> 50ms for BlueParcel model profile.
- Increase priority-lane slot cap by 30% on affected clusters (us-east-1/eu-west-1 routing group).
- Enable fallback to LOW_COST model variant for calls exceeding 2s latency as a mitigation.

We need BlueParcel to validate after 10–15 minutes whether errors reduce. I'll follow up with an internal playbook and RCA candidate. Marcus/Jonas/Laura — can you join and confirm rollback thresholds and a plan if changes worsen throughput?

— Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T08:02:00Z
Subject: FW: Production P0: BlueParcel — early internal notes

Forwarding Samir's thread and Kimberly's interim actions. Quick internal notes from my side after looking at the kv-eviction-graph.png (attached by Marcus in the internal doc):

Observations:
- Eviction spikes line up with requests that target a 3–4 specific prefix buckets — classic hot-key scenario.
- Prefetch windows appear to cause simultaneous loads for nearly-identical prefixes leading to hot eviction and HOL blocking.
- When eviction occurs on the priority lane we see cascading head-of-line (HOL) blocking for in-flight slots leading to 502/504s.

Immediate asks for eng: can we throttle concurrent prefetch workers for BlueParcel (limit concurrency per prefix) and backoff aggressive KV writes until the hot buckets stabilize? Also confirm whether the metric "kv.prefetch.clobber_count" can be exposed to the customer dashboard in a matter of hours.

I'm keeping Evelyn in the loop due to potential executive escalation (BlueParcel has an upcoming renewal/expansion next quarter).

— Laura

From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
To: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T09:05:00Z
Subject: Re: FW: Production P0: BlueParcel — early internal notes

Digging into the runtime traces and eviction histograms. Key technical points: 

- The prefetch policy we shipped uses a global async window that unfortunately schedules speculative loads for similar prefixes without per-prefix dedupe. With the current slot cap and hot-lane occupancy this results in near-simultaneous KV insertions and thrashing.
- HOL blocking shows up when a hot prefix triggers eviction of a token-set that other in-flight requests need; those requests get queued behind a lock waiting for the KV write/replication and then timeout.

Mitigation plan (rolling, low-risk):
1) Per-prefix prefetch dedupe: quick patch to check active prefetches for a prefix and skip duplicates. Rollout to BlueParcel routing group (canary 10% -> 50% -> 100%) — target 30m to full canary if metrics look good.
2) Reduce prefetch concurrency: set prefetch_concurrency = 4 (was 12) for BlueParcel profile. This is already staged and can be applied in 5m.
3) Backoff aggressive KV writes: change write_coalesce window from 50ms -> 200ms to batch small writes and reduce eviction churn.

If any step increases tail latency, we will immediately revert per the rollback thresholds below. I recommend we also expose kv.prefetch.clobber_count and kv.eviction.rate to the BlueParcel dashboard.

Rollback thresholds: p95 increase > 10% OR 5xx > +1% absolute for 5m window.

I'll push the prefetch_concurrency change now.

— Marcus
Senior Software Engineer, Serving Runtime

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.ai>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T11:46:00Z
Subject: Exec: BlueParcel P0 update and recommended customer-facing position

Evelyn — escalating to you because BlueParcel is a top-tier account and this incident may require Executive touch if customer sentiment worsens. Summary: 
- Impact window started ~07:10 UTC; peak 5xx ~12%; sustained p99 ~4.3s.
- Root cause hypothesis: prefetched speculative loads + per-profile slot caps causing KV eviction thrash and HOL blocking.

Actions taken: prefetch window reduction (Kim), prefetch_concurrency reduction (Marcus), priority-lane slot cap increased + switched long calls to fallback variant. Monitoring shows a partial improvement (5xx down to ~3.6%) but p99 still elevated in some zones.

Recommended exec actions:
- Offer BlueParcel a credit for the incident day (6–8 hours of usage credit) and a joint post-incident review within 48 hours.
- Temporarily open a dedicated hotlane shard for BlueParcel until we ship the per-prefix dedupe fix (estimated 36–48 hours to fully roll out).

I'll be on the call with the account at 18:00 UTC to walk through next steps if we need to.

— Jonas

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Shah <samir@blueparcel.com>
Cc: Marta Rodriguez <marta@blueparcel.com>, BlueParcel EngOps <ops@blueparcel.com>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.ai>
Date: 2026-11-18T18:42:00Z
Subject: Re: Production P0: 500 spikes + throughput collapse (many requests timing out) — mitigation applied

Samir —

Thanks for your patience. We applied the staged mitigations this morning: reduced prefetch window, lowered prefetch concurrency, and increased priority-lane capacity. Marcus also enabled per-prefix prefetch dedupe in canary which is at 50% for your routing group. Early telemetry shows 5xx down to ~1.1% and p99 reduced to ~1.1–1.5s for most routes. We will:

- Keep the canary running and push to 100% only after 2 hours of stable metrics.
- Provision a temporary dedicated hotlane shard if we see a relapse.
- Prepare a post-incident report with timeline, root cause, and permanent remediation (per-prefix dedupe + smarter slot autoscaling).

Please validate on your side and tell us if you still see checkout errors. If you prefer, we can join an immediate bridge.

Apologies for the impact — we're treating this as a P0. I'll follow up with a formal RCA and proposed customer credits as Jonas recommended.

— Kimberly
Sr. Manager, Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference
